title: Chapter 82 — Protection Plans: The Honest Framework
intro: Extended warranty selling done right — honest information, real value, no pressure.

sections.title: The Honest Approach
sections.content:
Extended warranties are the highest-margin product on your floor. They are also the most objected-to. The difference between a 20 percent attach rate and a 40 percent attach rate is not pressure — it is honesty.

Never say 'you should really get the warranty.' That is lazy selling. Instead: 'Here is what the manufacturer covers and for how long. Here is what happens after that coverage ends. The extended plan covers these specific things for this many years and it costs this amount. For a $2,000 dishwasher, that is about $X per month over the life of the plan. Whether it is worth it depends on how risk-tolerant you are.'

Give them the real information. Let them decide. If the product is unreliable and you know it, you should not be selling it in the first place — not compensating with warranty.

sections.title: Every Objection Answered
sections.content:
'I never buy warranties.' Response: 'I respect that. Most people feel the same way — until the compressor fails in year 3. Let me just show you what it covers so you can make an informed decision. Fair?'

'The manufacturer warranty should cover it.' Response: 'It does — for 1 to 5 years depending on the component. After that, you are on your own. A compressor replacement runs $800-$1,200. The plan is $X and covers it for additional years.'

'It costs too much.' Response: break it down monthly and compare to a single service call. The math often speaks for itself.

'I will use my credit card warranty.' Response: acknowledge it, then explain the gap — credit card plans typically add one year and require upfront payment with 60-90 day reimbursement.

sections.title: Presentation Timing
sections.content:
Present the warranty AFTER they have committed to the product but BEFORE the write-up. Do not lead with it. Do not hide it. Do not skip it. One honest presentation on every sale. Let the customer decide.

The rep who presents honestly on every sale at 35 percent conversion makes more money than the rep who pushes hard and converts at 25 percent — because the honest rep still has the customer relationship for the next purchase.
